title: unified-rollouts: add observability + stability guards for canary/shadow auto-rollback
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add rollout observability metrics and safety guards for automated canary/shadow rollouts; improvements to alerting and e2e stability tests; no breaking API changes.
description:
Background: Automated canary + shadow rollouts are the default rollout primitive for model lifecycle but we've seen incidents where insufficient observability and weak stability guards led to slow detection and expensive rollbacks. This PR introduces a focused set of observability metrics, dashboard wiring, and safety guards (quarantine/quorum) that the autorollback engine uses to make safer decisions.

Motivation: improve time-to-detection for regressions, reduce false-positive rollbacks, and provide clear runbook signals for SRE and platform teams.

Changes:
- Add rollout-level telemetry: rollout.request_count, rollout.latency_p50/90/99, rollout.error_rate, rollout.quality_regressions (per-eval-set counters) and rollout.metric_quorum status.
- Emit delta metrics on candidate vs baseline for key SLOs to simplify alerting and automated decision making.
- Integrate metric quorum and quarantine windows into the autorollback engine; quorum ensures at least N independent metrics must trigger before a hard rollback, quarantine applies short-term soft-fail state (traffic frozen at canary percent) while additional sampling runs.
- Add configuration knobs: rollout.observability.quorum_threshold, rollout.observability.quorum_window, rollout.safety.quarantine_duration, rollout.safety.max_soft_rollbacks. Defaults chosen conservatively based on field trials.
- Dashboard and alerting: wire new metrics into the unified-rollouts dashboard (canary overview) and add two alert rules (rollout:regression-high, rollout:metric-quorum-failed) with suggested runbook links.
- Tests and e2e: new unit tests for metric aggregation, integration tests that exercise quarantine/quorum transitions, and an e2e canary stability test that runs against the perf-canary harness.
- Docs: update rollout docs explaining observability metrics, recommended thresholds, and migration notes.

Checklist:
- [x] Telemetry schema + emitting hooks implemented
- [x] Autorollback engine uses quorum/quarantine logic
- [x] Dashboards updated and linked
- [x] Unit + integration + e2e tests added
- [x] Docs and runbooks updated

Design notes: The quorum implementation keeps a sliding-window bitmap of metric health signals (success/fail) and applies a simple majority rule with a configurable threshold. Quarantine is a timed state that prevents full traffic promotion until either metrics recover or quarantine expires; during quarantine traffic is pinned to the current canary ratio to limit blast radius. The metric delta buckets are coarse-grained to avoid high-cardinality metrics: we emit +/- bins relative to baseline for latency and error-rate.

Backwards compatibility: all new metrics are additive and opt-in via feature flag rollout.features.observability_v2; default is enabled for new rollouts only.

Migration: existing active rollouts will continue under previous logic until they are patched or recreated.

Testing performed:
- Local unit tests and mocked metric ingestion
- Integration tests with the rollout-sim harness to validate quarantine -> recover/rollback transitions
- Perf-canary run with a synthetic regression to ensure detection within expected windows
- Manual dashboard review with SRE to confirm alert thresholds

Review notes: initial CI run failed on linting formatting in rollout/metrics/registry.go; fixed in second commit. QA requested more graceful logging around quarantine transitions — added structured events for quarantine.enter/exit with rollout_id and reason. Observability/Infra requested a low-cardinality schema which is respected by using delta bins and tag minimization.

Commits summary: "initial commit: telemetry schema and emitters; autorollback: add quorum/quarantine engine; tests: unit/integration/e2e; docs: rollout observability + runbook; fix: lint/format; fix: reduce metric cardinality"

Merge rationale: changes are additive, tested across unit/integration/e2e, and required to reduce production incident surface for rollout regressions.

Merge method: squash.
